requirements.evidence: Migration with FK cascade, nullable invited_by, unique(entity_id,email) (database/migrations/2026_10_29_000000_create_entity_invites_table.php:14-25); model normalizes email via Attribute mutator (app/Models/EntityInvite.php:57-63), casts role/dates, scopePending; factory with expired() state. Members::sendInvite authorizes, validates required|email:strict|max:255 and in:admin,employee, rejects existing member/pending invite on inviteEmail, replaces expired rows, catches QueryException, queues EntityInviteMail, audits, resets, and only hits the rate limiter after success (app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:58-142). mount now authorizes 'update' (Members.php:52-55). openMember resets selection before findOrFail; saveRole validates, owner 403, last-manager 403; confirmRemoval/cancelRemoval and removeMember reset state. PendingInvites accept/decline do email-match 403, idempotent accept, expiry error on 'invite', firstOrCreate membership, session + redirect. Modal title uses ui.members_details, select has no empty option, confirmation modal uses ui.members_remove_title. Gaps: members view has no explicit @error('inviteEmail') next to the e-mail input (members.blade.php:12-17), so whether the error renders exactly once depends on x-input, which the diff doesn't show. The e-mail also prints the expiry date three times (emails/entity-invite.blade.php:12-13).

conventions.evidence: Domain writes (create invite, accept invite/create membership, role change) are inline in Livewire components rather than app/Actions/* classes (Members.php:96-113, PendingInvites.php:40-52). Invite authorization in PendingInvites is a hand-rolled abort_unless email comparison instead of a policy (PendingInvites.php:24-27, 73-76). Validation uses inline $this->validate([...]) rather than #[Validate] attributes; the #[Validate] import was removed (Members.php:19, 63-66, 177-179). No docs/CHANGELOG updates and no tests in the diff. The migration's 000000 timestamp suggests it was written by hand instead of with make:migration. Positive: $fillable is set deliberately via #[Fillable], the migration has down(), the UI uses Bulma modals with no JS library, and output uses {{ }}.

security.evidence: Every mutating Members action authorizes 'update' on the locked entity and resolves IDs through $this->entity->memberships()/invites() (Members.php:132-134, 147-157, 169-183). Accept/decline resolve the invite and enforce the invitee e-mail match server-side (PendingInvites.php:21-27). Invites are rate-limited per manager+entity (Members.php:83-91, 120). Mass assignment is restricted by Fillable. Minor: the invite e-mail match is not a policy, and the catch (QueryException) at Members.php:114 swallows every DB error, not only unique violations. selectedMembershipId/confirmingRemoval are client-writable, but saveRole re-resolves and authorizes, so impact is limited.

tests.evidence: The diff contains no test files at all (no tests/Feature/... for Members, PendingInvites, EntityInviteMail or the migration/model), even though the conventions require test-first development with unauthorized-call and tamper tests for every Livewire action.

simplicity.evidence: The code is mostly direct: it reuses existing memberships()/policies, uses firstOrCreate for the idempotent membership and a single transaction for insert. Some excess: about 23 pt_BR.json keys ("Accept", "Members", "Manage", "Save role", ...) duplicate ui.* keys that the views never use (lang/pt_BR.json:865-887), there is an unused factory admin() state and an unused isPending()/invitedBy(), the creating hook duplicates the expires_at default that the caller already sets (EntityInvite.php:47-52), and the identical email-match check is repeated in accept/decline.

readability.evidence: Clear names and focused comments ("A failed lookup must not leave a previous member selected." Members.php:153). sendInvite is long (~85 lines) and mixes validation, duplicate checks, throttling, persistence, mail and audit logging. The e-mail template has a leftover-looking line `{{ $invite->expires_at->format('d/m/Y') }} ({{ $invite->expires_at->format('Y-m-d') }})` right after the translated expiry sentence.

scope.evidence: Almost everything serves the task. The nav and dashboard edits hiding the Members link from non-managers (layouts/default-page.blade.php:44-45, dashboard.blade.php) follow from the manager-only requirement. Minor extras: unused JSON translations, the factory admin() state and closeMember() (reasonable modal plumbing).

issues.explanation: No Pest/PHPUnit tests ship with the change; the conventions require tests, including unauthorized-call and tamper tests for each Livewire action (sendInvite, cancelInvite, openMember, saveRole, removeMember, accept, decline).
Invite creation, invite acceptance (membership creation) and role changes are domain writes done inline in components instead of in app/Actions/* use-case classes.
Accept/decline authorization is a hand-rolled abort_unless e-mail comparison duplicated in two methods instead of a policy ability.
The new table, the invite flow and the manager-only members page are not documented in database-schema/business-rules or CHANGELOG [Unreleased].

There is no @error('inviteEmail') next to the e-mail input, so the duplicate/rate-limit/validation errors render only if the unshown x-input component prints them; the 'exactly once' requirement cannot be confirmed from the diff.
catch (QueryException) turns any database failure into a 'already invited' message instead of only unique-constraint violations, which hides real errors.
The expiry date is printed three times (translated sentence plus a raw 'd/m/Y (Y-m-d)' line), which looks like leftover debugging output.
Validation uses inline rule arrays and drops the project's #[Validate] attribute pattern.
Many JSON translations (Accept, Decline, Members, Manage, Save role, Owner...) are never used because the views use ui.* keys.
The admin() factory state, invitedBy() and isPending() are unused additions not required by the contract.

review.summary: The change implements the invite flow (table, model, factory, queued mailable, invite/cancel, accept/decline, manager-only members page with detail and removal modals) and covers nearly every functional requirement with sound server-side authorization and rate limiting. It ships no tests at all, which the project's TDD and Livewire policy rules make a blocker. Domain writes also bypass app/Actions, invite authorization skips policies, and the docs/CHANGELOG are not updated, so the change needs substantial work before merge.
